Yana: Quick follow-up on the header-first streaming idea — can we add a tiny optional 'warmup_priority' hint to safetensors headers (e.g. single byte or small flag per shard) so the loader can start hydrating high-priority layers earlier? Sketch below.

Yana: ```
# hypothetical header snippet
warmup_priority: 0..255  # larger => hydrate earlier
warmup_signature: optional-sig
```

Eli: I like the idea for low-latency tails, but how do we avoid breaking existing loaders? Optional field + strict unknown-field ignoring?

Jordan: Optional + versioned header field + loaders should ignore unknown attrs. My bigger concern is abuse: anyone could set priority=255 and starve other requests.

Kyle: Agreed. Two-tier approach: 1) lightweight header_hint (advisory) for permissive clients; 2) signed sidecar manifest (authoritative) for tenants that need QoS. Also cap header hints for unauthenticated sources.

loader-bot: ERROR parsing warmup_priority in shard-42, falling back to default priority=16 :warning:

Yana: Exactly — proposal: header_hint (advisory) + sidecar manifest (signed, authoritative). Heuristics: if header_hint > 200 and no valid manifest, cap to 64 to avoid abuse.

Eli: How do we express per-layer vs per-shard priority? Some layers (attn KV) need to be hydrated before embeddings/FFN to reduce tail latency.

Yana: Suggest warmup_scope syntax — tiny enumerations in header for common cases, full JSON in sidecar. Examples: `warmup_scope: "attn_kv,head0..head15"` for header-friendly; full sidecar can be: {"priority":200, "scopes":[{"type":"layer","name":"attn_kv"},{"type":"range","start":0,"end":3}]}.

Jordan: Also think about eviction interplay — loader must reserve warmup_budget and not OOM. We need a global per-node budget and per-request caps.

Kyle: Start conservative: default per-loader warmup_budget = 128MB (configurable), reservation expires after 30s if not used. Telemetry: `warmup_duration_ms`, `priority_used`, `hint_source` (header|sidecar|none).

Eli: Tests we should add: header parsing unit tests, integration sim that injects malicious headers to ensure caps/truncation/capping logic works.

Yana: I'll draft a short RFC: header-advisory + signed-manifest + caps + telemetry + e2e checklist. Minimal migration story: old loaders ignore fields; new loaders expose `warmup_hint_seen` telemetry. @Kyle do you want to own the loader change? :+1:

Kyle: I can take it. I'll open a PR with parser + cap logic + basic telemetry + fallback behavior. Plan: feature-flag behind `warmup_hints_enabled` until RFC approved.

Jordan: :thumbsup: also add metric `warmup_fallback_to_manifest` so we can measure how often headers are ignored in favor of signed manifests.

loader-bot: Scheduled job created: warmup-cap-simulation #1234

Yana: Cool — thanks all. I'll drop the RFC link when ready.
